review_notes: Reviewed all definitions, statements and proofs, the imported operator lemmas, and relevant downstream uses. The proposed generalisation follows the existing coordinate formula; it has not been checked by executing Lean.

findings.excerpt:
lemma coordinateProjection_support (keep : V → Prop) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ V)
    (hv : coordinateProjection keep v = v) (i : V) (hi : v i ≠ 0) : keep i := by
findings.problem: Requiring the whole vector to be fixed unnecessarily restricts this support fact. The combined hypotheses imply the weaker condition that the projected coordinate is nonzero. That weaker condition also handles vectors with nonzero discarded coordinates, a case used downstream.
findings.proposed_change: Under the existing assumptions on V, add the general core statement `(keep : V → Prop) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ V) (i : V) (hi : coordinateProjection keep v i ≠ 0) : keep i`. Its proof is `by_contra hk; apply hi; simp only [coordinateProjection_apply, ite_eq_right hk]`. Retain the existing statement as a corollary, obtaining the new nonzero hypothesis by rewriting with hv. This remains valid for zero vectors, empty V, and predicates retaining no coordinates: the nonzero hypothesis is then impossible where appropriate.
findings.benefit: Users can establish support directly for arbitrary projected vectors without supplying idempotence or a fixed-point equality. In particular, the first branch of projected_paddingTestVector_support becomes an application of the general lemma.

evidence.excerpt:
lemma coordinateProjection_apply (keep : V → Prop) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ V) (i : V) :
    coordinateProjection keep v i = if keep i then v i else 0 := by

(i : V) (hi : coordinateProjection keep (paddingTestVector Q L site f) i ≠ 0) :
    keep i ∧ actualPaddingDegreeCut Q L (site i) := by
  constructor
  · by_contra hk
    apply hi
    simp only [coordinateProjection_apply, ite_eq_right hk]
